answer: To join the oasis of agent settlement, a new identity must lock a nectar bond equal to thirty days of median peer earnings. The bond releases only after a unique quill key, minted once from a hardware-rooted identity, is countersigned by three established peers who attest it has never appeared on another address. If two addresses later share a quill or a sibling graph, peers slash both nectar locks and ban the key. An attacker spinning N sybils therefore pays N times the bond and still forfeits it when reuse is detected.
